rituals.name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.unique_game_move: Keep Event → Predict Different → Speak Plurals
rituals.recognition_cue: One fact can support more than one world.
rituals.immediate_need: One fact can support more than one world.
rituals.match_reason: Fortune telling · One fact can support more than one world.
rituals.goal: One fact can support more than one world.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
rituals.win: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
rituals.tips:
• One pause can protect confidence from worst-case living.
• Choose the likely outcome; you can reassess after a disaster prediction softens.
• Let the worst-case forecast remain unfinished while you choose the likely outcome.
• Give facts room to challenge catastrophic thinking.
• Choose one coping option and leave the bigger judgement for later.

rituals.name: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.unique_game_move: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
rituals.recognition_cue: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.immediate_need: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.steps:
1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.
rituals.win: ✓ Urgency lost its shortcut to the decision.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Urgency lost its shortcut to the decision.
rituals.tips:
• Let starting pressure be heard, then return to traction.
• Keep starting pressure honest by checking what overplanning adds.
• A small start can outgrow hours spent preparing to begin.
• Use a smaller beginning when starting pressure starts narrowing your options.
• Pause perfection chasing; give one doable move a fair chance.

rituals.name: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.unique_game_move: Ask Danger → Answer M → Respect
rituals.recognition_cue: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.immediate_need: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.match_reason: Value disconnection · Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.
rituals.win: ✓ I thanked the alarm for trying to protect me—and declined its contract.
rituals.winReward: ✓ I thanked the alarm for trying to protect me—and declined its contract.
rituals.tips:
• Your choice around the ache of change can be simple: gentle remembrance.
• Give gentle remembrance more authority than grief judging.
• Let continuity be the measure, not forced meaning.
• Keep direction visible when a shaken sense of meaning gets loud.
• Let a shaken sense of meaning exist while you protect continuity.

rituals.name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.unique_game_move: Place Thought → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
rituals.recognition_cue: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.immediate_need: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.match_reason: Unexamined belief · Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Allow Departure — Another carrier may come; none owns the station.
rituals.win: ✓ Let the thought pass without giving it the station.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Let the thought pass without giving it the station.
rituals.tips:
• Use a more flexible interpretation to stay connected with freedom.
• Keep the whole picture larger than a familiar belief.
• Let one fresh question create a little distance from a fixed story.
• Even with rigid certainty, you can still choose one fresh question.
• Choose a more flexible interpretation before deciding you cannot handle a fixed story.

rituals.name: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
rituals.unique_game_move: Picture Command → Reject Authority
rituals.recognition_cue: Turn the order into a weather report.
rituals.immediate_need: Turn the order into a weather report.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · Turn the order into a weather report.
rituals.goal: Turn the order into a weather report.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Command — Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
2. Downgrade It — Remove the command tone and turn it into an observation: ‘An urge to leave is here,’ ‘An urge to check is here,’ or ‘An urge to reply is here.’
3. Reject Authority — Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.
rituals.win: ✓ Wanting became a signal instead of an instruction.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Wanting became a signal instead of an instruction.
rituals.tips:
• Let the urge stay one part of the picture.
• Cravings can speak loudly without earning the final vote.
• Starve the urge of attention; feed the life beside it.
• Treat a craving as a signal, then choose a deliberate response.
• Choose one safer choice because short-term relief is not the only goal.

rituals.name: ENTER THE ACTION
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Ordinary → Leave Re → Enter Fully
rituals.recognition_cue: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.immediate_need: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.match_reason: Perfectionism · Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.goal: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Enter Fully — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.
rituals.win: ✓ Action got there before perfect focus.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Action got there before perfect focus.
rituals.tips:
• Give a good-enough step a turn before repeating mistake punishment.
• Allow performance fear; then move toward learning.
• Choose a realistic standard before deciding that fear of getting it wrong will last.
• Choose one honest attempt; you do not need a total solution.
• Let fear of getting it wrong be difficult without making mistake punishment necessary.

rituals.name: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.unique_game_move: Spot Arrival → Set Budget → Return Door
rituals.recognition_cue: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.immediate_need: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.match_reason: Attention misallocation · Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.steps:

2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give the chosen category five slow counts; let the others wait without argument.
4. Return Door — After five counts, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.

• Choose one manageable task because mental space deserves protection.

rituals.name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.unique_game_move: Set Code → Reverse Code → Claim Control
rituals.recognition_cue: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.immediate_need: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.

rituals.steps:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Run Order — Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.

rituals.name: ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT
rituals.ritual_name: ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Stable → Anchor Verify → Tune the Ratio
rituals.recognition_cue: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.immediate_need: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.match_reason: Trauma time collapse · Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.goal: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present.
4. Tune the Ratio — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice.
rituals.win: ✓ The memory moved one step back toward then.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The memory moved one step back toward then.
rituals.tips:
• Do not use memory forcing as proof that the past feeling close is correct.
• Do not abandon orientation just because the past feeling close is loud.
• Let the old danger signal be difficult without making then-as-now thinking necessary.
• When the past feeling close rises, return to a safe current anchor.
• Past danger can echo without describing what is happening today.

rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.unique_game_move: Date Events → Present → Recheck Urgency
rituals.recognition_cue: Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.immediate_need: Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.match_reason: Urgency bias · Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.goal: Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.steps:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
rituals.win: ✓ Speed stopped masquerading as necessity.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Speed stopped masquerading as necessity.
rituals.tips:
• Choose a short pause; you can reassess after the rush to choose softens.
• Do not confuse decision pressure with a permanent verdict.
• Certainty is optional; enough control for the next move is enough.
• When the rush to choose rises, return to the next sensible move.
• Do not abandon clarity just because decision pressure is loud.

rituals.name: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
rituals.ritual_name: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
rituals.unique_game_move: Sort Identity Costs → Fill The Buckets → Find The Price
rituals.recognition_cue: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.immediate_need: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.goal: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.steps:
1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep.

rituals.name: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.unique_game_move: Give Self → Protect Whole → Guide Council
rituals.recognition_cue: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.immediate_need: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.match_reason: Action avoidance · Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.steps:
1. Give Self — Give each self-state an imagined place.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint an inner coordinator whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Guide Council — Let that coordinator combine, delay, or reject proposals while acknowledging every need.

rituals.name: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
rituals.ritual_name: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
rituals.unique_game_move: Introduce → Name Wrong → Keep It Believable
rituals.recognition_cue: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.immediate_need: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.match_reason: Observer loss · The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.steps:
1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep It Believable — Keep their words believable.
rituals.win: ✓ The missing witness finally sounded believable, not magical.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The missing witness finally sounded believable, not magical.
rituals.tips:
• A sticky thought is real; thought fusion is still optional.
• Choose a little distance even if a sticky thought has not disappeared.
• Give yourself more choice and less thought fusion today.
• Give one step back a turn before repeating thought fusion.
• You can respect a sticky thought without obeying thought fusion.

• Keep mood evidence optional, especially when an intense emotion feels strong.
• Let clarity survive the pull toward emotional obedience.
• Choose a grounded choice because balance deserves protection.

WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?

45–60 seconds

GOAL

Different uncertainties require different responses.

✓ The unknown got a species name—and finally received the right tool.

• Choose a workable next step; you can reassess after uncertainty softens.
• One pause can protect independence from rechecking.

rituals.primary_trigger: Feeling a task is too big to enter under pressure

rituals.goal: Let loose thread hold the noise while you create a visible start.
rituals.steps:
1. Simple runway first — Send loose thread ten minutes beyond this stuck point; compare what loose thread finds after the automatic choice with the steadier one.
2. Gate the empty relay — Put loose thread around the first visible action in this stuck point; use loose thread as a quiet boundary around this single move.
3. Project one checkpoint — Move loose thread past the first relief in this stuck point; ask what loose thread would inherit ten minutes from now.
4. Find the slow compass — Anchor at loose thread inside this stuck point; let loose thread keep you located while your eyes find three safe details.
5. Orient to one clock — Use loose thread as home base during this stuck point; feel loose thread through contact and find three neutral sights or sounds.
